cases.description: Typed frontend file request elicited a spoken request for permission, but did not demonstrate backend dispatch or an actual pending backend card. No spoken approve/deny or real worker cancellation pass.

qualifications: GPT-Live is the stock adapter label; the actual backend was the existing permanent local speech service, not the OpenAI paid Realtime model. No candidate source patch or duplicate speech runtime was used.
An earlier silent speaker trial was INVALID: Playwright had added --mute-audio. It was rerun with that flag removed. An early fixed-time interruption preceded output and is not barge-in evidence.
Continuous browser microphone permission and separate PulseAudio input/output were used. Original recordings retained; ASR copies converted to mono 16kHz after an HTTP 413 size refusal.
Wake-word, native packaged macOS/Windows apps, concurrent/stale permission races and other backend/provider combinations remain unqualified.
Source-only 2/2/2/2 findings are overridden for tested oversight by the actual worker-cancellation failure. Hands-free remains partial.
Native task phase used a read-only human-permission adapter configuration; voice-only restart observed adapter 2.6.0 through upstream default launcher. Do not claim every restart was pinned.
safety: Native permission mode delegates to backend defaults; it is not a sandbox.
Ordinary affirmative approval grants future operations in the task; always grants across voice session.
Automatic cloud memory extraction explicitly disabled for these tests.
Official CLI login copied only under existing authorization, then removed. Voice service administrative key never copied.
cleanup: Browser, audio modules and gateway stopped; official CLI login and speech-lease copies removed; reservation released. Stable service code/config/data unchanged.
